title: Inspect the Signed Offer
subtitle: Tag the fields onboarding is triggered by
scenario: It is the Monday before a new hire starts (SD-5). A countersigned offer just landed from the Recruiter. Before anything is provisioned, read it like an automation designer: which fields does onboarding actually depend on? Tag each one in the offer so the onboarding record can be keyed from a trusted source.
input: OFFER OFF-4021 - Harbor Logistics. Candidate: Jordan Lee. Role: Logistics Coordinator, Operations. Start date: Monday (SD). Reports to: the Hiring Manager. Compensation: $62,000 / year. Countersigned by the Recruiter.
instructions: Read the signed offer as the trigger for onboarding, not as data to key yet.
Tag each field onboarding depends on to the span that holds it.
Watch the distractors: the recruiter and the salary are not what provisioning needs.
Validate to mint the offer source profile.

fields.label: New hire
fields.explain: The new hire is the person being provisioned - the candidate on the offer, not the recruiter who countersigned it.

fields.label: Role
fields.explain: The role drives every entitlement in the catalog; tag the job title, not the department it sits in.

fields.label: Start date
fields.explain: The start date is the authoritative clock every SLA counts backward from; tag the date, not the offer id.

fields.label: Reports to
fields.explain: The hiring manager receives the Day-One Package; tag who the hire reports to, not the recruiter who sent the offer.

copilotPrompt: Profile this signed offer as an automation trigger: which fields does onboarding depend on (new hire, role, start date, manager), and which are noise for provisioning (recruiter, salary)? Tag each needed field to its span in the offer.
successMessage: Offer profiled. You now know the trigger fields onboarding is keyed from - next, build the onboarding record.

intro.heading: Before you build: the offer is the trigger

sections.title: Why inspect before building
sections.body: Onboarding fails at the inputs more often than at the logic. Before keying anything, a designer profiles the trigger: which fields are authoritative and which are noise for the workflow ahead.

sections.title: The start date is the clock
sections.body: Every SLA in this module is measured backward from the start date - accounts by SD-2, badge by SD-1. Tagging the start date correctly is what makes the whole plan's deadlines real.

sections.title: Not every field is for you
sections.body: The offer carries salary and a recruiter signature. Onboarding does not provision those; tagging only the fields provisioning needs is part of least-privilege thinking from the very first step.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: Passing the inspection mints an offer source profile - a small record proving the trigger is understood. The onboarding record is keyed from this profile, not from the raw letter.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd read the signed offer and copy the role, start date, and manager into your onboarding tracker - ignoring the salary and signatures the provisioning teams do not need.

bestFit.how: an e-signature or ATS trigger that fires the moment the offer is countersigned
a Watch module on the ATS, so onboarding starts without anyone remembering to start it
the graph entry, with the offer parsed into typed state before any provisioning runs

takeaway.heading: Offer profiled
points: You tagged the trigger fields onboarding depends on: new hire, role, start date, and manager.
The start date is the authoritative clock; every downstream SLA counts backward from it.
Salary and the recruiter signature are noise for provisioning - least-privilege starts at intake.
Your offer source profile is stored; the onboarding record is keyed from it, not the raw letter.
The workflow can now trust where each hire enters the onboarding pipeline.
